name: Empire line dress
summary: The high-waisted dress after the French Revolution: a light, straight muslin gown that falls from a seam under the bust, like Greek dress.

philosophy.core_thesis: After the Revolution, a dress drops the hoop and the stays and shows a light, straight line from a waist under the bust.
design_principles: Set the waist seam directly under the bust, about 10 cm above the natural waist.
Cut the skirt straight or slightly gored, and let it fall to the ankle in soft folds.
Make the day dress in white or pale muslin of 30 to 90 g per square metre.
Keep the neckline low and square or round, and the sleeve short and puffed.
Draw the bodice in with a cord or a ribbon under the bust.
Border the hem with a band of white embroidery, 15 to 30 cm deep.
Add a spencer jacket or a shawl for warmth; do not add a layer of petticoats.
anti_patterns: Wide side hoops and a stiff cone bodice
A waist at the natural line
Dark, saturated, strong colour for a day dress
A full train for a day dress
Boned stays that show a rigid line

silhouette.shape: A tall, narrow column: a short bodice, a waist just under the bust and a straight skirt to the ankle.
silhouette.line: A low neckline, a short puffed sleeve and an unbroken vertical fall of cloth from the bust to the hem.
silhouette.fit: Close at the bust where the seam sits, then free; the skirt hangs from the seam and shows the leg.
silhouette.proportion: Bodice about 15 cm long from shoulder seam to waist seam; skirt about 4 to 5 times the bodice; hem at the ankle.
rules: Place the waist seam under the bust, and draw it in with a cord.
Cut the skirt in straight panels so that it falls in vertical folds.
Keep the colour pale and the cloth fine; one layer is enough in a warm room.
Wear a short spencer jacket or a long shawl over the dress, not a cage or a hoop.
Border the hem and the neckline with a band of white or gold embroidery.

fabrics.rule: Choose a fine, light cloth that drapes: white muslin and cambric for day, satin and net for evening, velvet or twill outside.

methods: drawstring at the neck and the waist
straight panels gathered at the back
short stays or a front-laced bodice
hem band worked in white embroidery
construction.closures: Ties and drawstrings at the back; later buttons or hooks at the back of the bodice.
construction.details: Puff sleeves, a low neckline, a sash under the bust, a spencer jacket or a cashmere shawl, and a small turban or bonnet.

surface.pattern: White on white: sprigs and borders in tambour work on the muslin; evening dress in plain satin with a silver or gold trim.
surface.gloss: Muslin at 2–5 GU; satin evening dress at 40–60 GU.
surface.wear: Fine muslin tears and yellows; a dress is washed and re-starched, and fine pieces show mends.

palette.strategy: White and ivory for day; pale pastels and a single bold accent for evening.

processes: cutting straight panels from flat cloth
gathering at the neck and the waist
tambour embroidery of the hem band
starching and pressing of fine muslin
making.scale: Made by a dressmaker to order, or at home from a plate in a fashion journal; plain dresses are quick to make.
making.signs: A seam under the bust, drawstring ties, a deep white hem border, and cloth that falls in soft vertical folds.

pieces.form: White muslin day dress with a waist seam under the bust
Satin gown with a short sleeve and a net overskirt
Pelisse of silk twill, closed down the front
Short spencer jacket worn over the dress

emotion.target_response: A sense of lightness and clarity: the viewer sees white cloth, a high waist and a calm, classical line.

use_cases: a period costume brief for a Regency film or play
a bridal dress with a high waist
a fashion image prompt for a 1810 ball
a museum label for an early 19th century gown
avoid_when: the brief wants a fitted waist and a full skirt
the brief is Victorian or Edwardian dress
the brief needs rich, heavy silk

modifiers.how: Add hoops and stays, lower the waist, and switch from white muslin to flower brocade.
Move the waist down, widen the skirt on a cage, and add a coloured silk.

ornament_level.note: A day dress carries white embroidery at the hem only; an evening gown may carry metal thread.
